/Volumes/WorkSpace/vogle/herdr-gitdeck 은 Herdr 데스크톱 앱용 git 클라이언트 mod(gitdeck)이고, 지금 TypeScript로 작성해 main.js 하나로 번들하고 있어.
코드는 고치지 말고 분석 보고서만 써 줘.

알고 싶은 것:
1. Herdr mod를 Rust나 Go 같은 다른 언어로 만들 수 있는지. Herdr가 mod를 어떻게 불러오는지(JS 런타임? WASM? 네이티브 바이너리?)부터 확인해 줘.
   근거: ~/.config/herdr-app/AGENTS.md, herdr.d.ts, gpui-kit.d.ts, 이 저장소의 docs/DEVELOPMENT.md
2. 다른 사람들이 만든 Herdr mod는 무슨 언어로 만드는지. GitHub 토픽 herdr-mod와 herdr.dev/mods에서 몇 개를 실제로 확인해서, Rust로 만든 mod가 정말 많은지, 그렇다면 UI는 어떻게 그리는지(Rust로 별도 프로세스를 두고 JS가 감싸는 구조인지 등) 알려 줘.
3. 바꿀 수 있다면 Rust, Go, TypeScript(그대로) 중 무엇이 gitdeck에 가장 좋은지 비교해 줘.
   비교할 점: 성능(git 명령 호출이 대부분이라는 점 고려), 배포·설치 방법(OS마다 빌드가 필요한지), 자동 업데이트 기능과의 호환, 테스트(지금 326개, 커버리지 99%), 옮기는 데 드는 작업량, 보안(mod는 신뢰된 코드로 실행됨)
4. 결론: 추천 하나와 그 이유, 바꾸지 않는 게 낫다면 그것도 그대로 말해 줘.

확인한 사실과 추측은 나눠서 적고, 웹에서 본 내용은 출처 링크를 달아 줘. 답은 한국어로 해 줘.
</pasted_content id="f912">

1	# Herdr app
2	
3	<!-- Written by the Herdr app on every start. Edits here are overwritten. -->
4	
5	This folder is **the Herdr app's whole interface, as files**. The Herdr app
6	is a desktop app for terminals and coding agents, and it redraws itself from
7	these files while it runs: change a layout, a key or a panel here and the
8	window follows within a second. Shipped layouts and mods are Herdr's:
9	change settings for look, or clone before editing structure/code (see Layouts).
10	When someone asks for something ("a sidebar
11	of my PRs", "give ctrl+1 back to the shell", "make it warmer", "move the
12	agents list to the right"), you do it by editing these files or writing a
13	mod. Nothing in the default interface is special: the spaces sidebar, the
14	agents list, the tab bar, menus, dialogs and notifications are built
15	from the same parts you have.
16	
17	## Two programs
18	
19	- **`herdr-app`**, the window: spaces, tabs, layouts, panels.
20	- **herdr-core (`hc`)**, which runs every terminal and agent. They keep
21	  running when the window closes or updates. You can use `hc` yourself:
22	  start a terminal, read its screen, send it text, wait for an agent
23	  (`hc --help`). The Herdr app is one client of it.
24	
25	`herdr-app` controls this app; `hc` controls herdr-core.
26	
27	## What you can and can't do
28	
29	You can: rearrange and restyle the whole window (layouts), rebind any key,
30	write panels (mods) that list, filter and act on spaces, tabs, agents
31	and terminals, open dialogs, popups and floating blocks, show a live
32	terminal inside a block, run any app command, run programs (`exec`) and
33	fetch URLs, keep state per mod or shared between mods, animate natively.
34	
35	You can't: use HTML, CSS, a web view, Node APIs or `setTimeout`; draw
36	outside your block except through overlays; change how a terminal itself
37	draws text; read or change other mods' code at run time.
38	
39	## What mods are written in
40	
41	Mods use **gpui-kit** (its gpui-shell): JavaScript that describes **GPUI**
42	elements, a native GPU UI (`div()`, flex, children,
43	`.on_click`). There's no DOM: the script describes, Rust draws. Background:
44	https://gpui-kit.com. The Herdr app carries its own copy with additions
45	(`frames`, `loop`), so **the type files here are the truth**:
46	`gpui-kit.d.ts` for elements and `herdr.d.ts` for the app's data and
47	commands. They're rewritten on every start to match this version.
48	
49	## Changing things safely
50	
51	- Edits apply at once. If a file is invalid, the app keeps the last good
52	  version and writes why to `<name>.error` (`layout.error`, `keys.error`,
53	  `settings.error`, `programs.error`). Check after every edit.
54	- `herdr-app check <mod folder>` loads a mod once and checks its initial
55	  description and eager native elements, including virtual lists and motion.
56	  It does not lay out the mod or run deferred rows, nested renders, or later
57	  async states. Never call a mod done without a passing check; also try it
58	  in the app.
59	- **Escape hatch:** `ctrl-alt-shift-escape` always works: it sets the shown
60	  layout and `keys.json` aside (`*.reset-<time>`) and goes back to the
61	  default `main` layout. Nothing can rebind it.
62	
63	## Seeing the window
64	
65	`herdr-app shot [file.png]` saves the last rendered window frame as a PNG
66	and prints its absolute path (default: `herdr-shot.png` in your current
67	folder). Use it when debugging mod UIs: inspect spacing, colors, terminal
68	images, overlays, popups and floats. It captures the app, not the desktop,
69	at the window’s physical pixel size, even when covered or minimized. No
70	screen-recording permission is needed. Herdr must be running; before its
71	first frame or during GPU recovery it reports an error instead of a PNG.
72	`HERDR_APP_HOME` selects which running window to ask, as with `status`.
73	
74	## The files
75	
76	| File | What it decides | Applied |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| `layouts/<name>.json` | the window and its whole look: blocks, theme, fonts, backgrounds, pane frames; one file per layout (`main`, `terminals`, `win98`, any you add) | live |
79	| `keys.json` | what every key does | live |
80	| `settings.json` | the person: zoom, sounds, fonts for every layout | live |
81	| `mods/<name>/` | panels: small JavaScript programs | live (hot reload) |
82	| `programs.json` | how programs show (name, icon, tile), on top of the built-in table | live |
83	| `icons/` | the shipped program icons | written by Herdr (put your own elsewhere) |
84	| `frame/` | the app's own screens (welcome, ...) | rewritten by Herdr on every start: don't edit, it won't stick |
85	| `view.json` | this screen's selected space/tab/pane, zoom, settled tabs, recent spaces and seen attention | written by Herdr |
86	| `shared.json`, `data/`, `seen.json`, `installed.json`, `window.json`, `windows.json` | mod state, bookkeeping, where the window was (size, maximized), mods' windows (spots, kept ones) | written by Herdr |
87	
88	Shared state is saved atomically in the background, with the latest change winning.
89	If `shared.json` is invalid, Herdr logs a warning and keeps it as
90	`shared.json.corrupt-<time>` before starting empty.
91	`herdr-app check` uses empty shared state in memory and leaves this file untouched.
92	
93	## The model: spaces, tabs, terminals
94	
95	Every layout shows the same world; a layout may show less, never a
96	different one. Each machine keeps its spaces, tabs and splits in its core's
97	`herdr-app` document. Connected screens share that layout and live terminals,
98	not their focus, zoom or attention. Use commands to change structure; there
99	is no `spaces.json`. On simultaneous edits the newest accepted document wins
100	(no merging); structural commands fail while that machine's layout is unavailable.
101	Mod pane props are stored as given, never machine-qualified. Space order is local
102	machine first, then machines by name; `space.move` stays inside its machine's block.
103	In the expanded Spaces sidebar, drag a space to reorder it within its machine;
104	the highlighted line shows where it will land.
105	
106	- A **space** is a place to work, on one machine: this one, or another
107	  from `hc machine ls` (`spaces()[i].machine`). Herdr leaves out machines
108	  added with `--temp` (an agent's short-lived sandbox): no spaces, not in
109	  `machines()`, and mods listing machines skip `temporary`. Names work as in Herdr:
110	  a space nobody named is called after where its first terminal is now
111	  (its repo, else its folder, `~` at home) and follows it; once named
112	  (`space.rename`), the name stays; renaming to "" goes back.
113	  `spaces()[i].named` says which. Where a space is now is its terminals'
114	  live folders (`panes()[i].cwd`), not the folder it was made in: new
115	  tabs start where its focused pane is, and the default mods take a
116	  space's repo from its first terminal.
117	  If starting in an inherited folder fails, new spaces, tabs and splits retry in
118	  that machine's home. Explicit invalid folders still fail.
119	- A **tab** is a piece of work in a space: its terminals and how they're
120	  split right and down. One nobody named is called by its place (1, 2,
121	  ...), as in Herdr; `tab.rename` names it ("fix login"). A space
122	  has one or more; closing the last one closes the space (it stays in
123	  `recent`).
124	- A tab can be **settled** (`tab.settle`): put away on this screen, still running;
125	  `settled` on each tab. The shipped layouts don't use it (they list every
126	  tab); a mod that does can hide or fold settled tabs. Showing one, or an
127	  agent in it needing the user, brings it back.
128	- A **pane** is a terminal on screen, or a **mod** beside them (a markdown
129	  viewer, a board, a git panel): `pane.split {direction, mod, props}`. A
130	  mod pane splits, zooms, closes and gets a header like any pane, keeps
131	  the keyboard when clicked, and is saved with its tab; its `props` tell
132	  it what to show (a file, a folder). Closing a terminal pane ends its
133	  terminal, and a program exiting closes its pane, even if Herdr was closed.
134	  Terminal panes are kept by their machine's core (`keep: true`). A lost
135	  terminal (core crash, reboot, logout) gets a shell in its last folder,
136	  with the same address; its original command is never run again. Splits
137	  and mod panes stay. An exited or killed terminal is closed, not restarted.
138	  Focus, zoom, recent spaces, settled tabs and seen attention stay on this screen.
139	- Every terminal is a core terminal. Herdr labels the ones it starts with
140	  `herdr.space=<id>` and `herdr.tab=<id>`. **A terminal with those
141	  labels shows up there**, even one you start yourself:
142	  `hc run --keep --label herdr.space=<id> --label herdr.tab=<id> -- claude`.
143	  Labels use ids local to that machine; remote ids shown by the app have a
144	  `<machine>/` prefix (strip it when writing labels on that machine). Adoption
145	  also enables core keep; `terminal.park` removes the pane and disables keep.
146	  When a core change is needed, `terminal.keep` / `terminal.park` acknowledge
147	  with `pending: true`, then apply after the machine replies; failures show a toast.
148	  Normal quit waits for pending terminal changes and layout writes; remote waits are bounded.
149	  An id Herdr doesn't know becomes a new space or tab (unnamed: Herdr's names).
150	  Terminals without the labels (another app's) stay out of Herdr's
151	  screens, and so do other machines' terminals, unless Herdr started them
152	  for a space on that machine.
153	- **Agents** are terminals whose program reports a status (OSC 7501):
154	  `working`, `blocked`, `idle`, or `done` = finished while the user wasn't
155	  looking (it becomes `idle` once they look). A space's and a tab's
156	  status is the most urgent of its agents: blocked > done > working > idle.
157	- **Sub-agents** are terminals an agent started with `hc run`: the core
158	  records the starter as `parent` (see `terminals()`). Parent addresses use
159	  the app's machine names, or a bare ID for this computer, when they can be
160	  mapped; otherwise they stay as the core reported them. They belong to their
161	  parent's tab without a pane; the `agents` mod shows them,
162	  `terminal.peek` opens one, `terminal.keep` gives one a pane.
163	  Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on macOS) a live terminal address in terminal text to
164	  peek at it. Bare addresses refer to the machine of the terminal showing them;
165	  use `machine/address` for another machine. Names and non-live addresses aren't links.
166	- **Agent navigation order** belongs to the mods. A mod displaying agents calls
167	  `setAgentOrder(list.map(a => a.address))` on render so `agent.next` /
168	  `agent.prev` follow its list.
169	
170	## Layouts: `layouts/<name>.json`
171	
172	Each file is one whole window. `layout.switch` (`ctrl-shift-l`) cycles
173	through them, `layout.switch {name}` picks one; `shared("layout")` is the
174	shown one's name. Herdr ships `main` ("Herdr": spaces by machine and the
175	agents list on the left, `workspace-chrome`; tabs as pills with a + menu
176	that starts a terminal or any installed agent, `new-menu`; panes as cards
177	with a header; Files and Changes panels on the right, `files` and
178	`changes`, opened from the tab bar and remembered per space (which ones:
179	shared `"workspace.panels"`, set by the welcome); a status bar,
180	`workspace-status`), and as examples `terminals` ("Terminals": tabs in
181	the title bar, panes as cards, a space picker) and `win98`
182	("Herdr 98": a whole desktop in one mod, `win98`). Add a layout by
183	writing a new file. The Files panel supports Windows folder paths with spaces,
184	parentheses and apostrophes, and preserves Unicode file and folder names
185	(including Chinese). Directory links expand as folders; their contents load
186	only when expanded.
187	
188	**Herdr's own layouts and mods are read-only.** They are replaced whole
189	on every start. Use settings.json for look (fonts, sizes, theme, colors,
190	sounds), where the layout leaves them unset. Herdr (main) has no look of
191	its own, so your settings decide it; Herdr 98 and Terminals bring their own
192	look. The theme picker overrides any layout. To change a shipped layout's
193	look beyond that, or its structure/code, clone it and edit the clone:
194	
195	```sh
196	herdr-app do layout.clone '{"name":"main","as":"my-layout"}'
197	herdr-app do mod.clone '{"name":"files","as":"my-files"}'
198	```
199	
200	The default clone name is `<name>-copy`; an existing name is refused.
201	`layout.clone` switches to the clone. In the palette: Duplicate layout
202	or Duplicate mod. Clones are yours and never updated. They record
203	`cloned_from: {name, version}` and copy the layout and its clicks as-is,
204	including its look. A cloned layout keeps its mod references:
205	clone a mod too and point your layout's `content.mod` to it to change code.
206	Mod clones rewrite their own `mods/<name>/` asset paths and self-opening
207	overlay names to the new name.
208	
209	If you edit a shipped file anyway, the next start moves it to
210	`<name>-edited` (a mod folder or layout JSON; a number is added if taken),
211	copies its layout clicks, restores Herdr's version and shows a toast.
212	No-longer-shipped things go if
213	untouched, otherwise they stay.
214	
215	Clicks (sizes, shown/hidden, stack child, floating spots, theme picks,
216	background, text size, pane header height and border/focus look) live
217	in `layouts/.state/` and survive restarts. Don't edit those files.
218	A deliberate layout-file edit beats a click on that field.
219	`layout.reset {name}` resets a shipped layout and its clicks, keeping its
220	previous file aside as `<name>.json.old-<time>`.
221	
222	A layout is a tree of nodes. Four types:
223	
224	- `block`: shows content. `"content"` is `{ "mod": "<folder>", "props": {...} }`,
225	  `{ "terminal": "t7" }`, `{ "tab": "active" }` (the shown tab's
226	  terminals as it arranges them), or `{ "agent": "focused" }` (one agent's
227	  terminal, full size: the one chosen with `agent.focus` / `agent.next`, else
228	  the focused pane's agent, else the first agent).
229	- `row` / `column`: children side by side / stacked.
230	- `stack`: shows one child (`"active": "<child id>"`), with an optional
231	  `"header"` (a mod that draws tabs, or `"tabs"` for a plain built-in strip).
232	
233	Properties any node can have:
234	- `id` (unique; commands use it), `size`: `{ "px": 240 }` or `{ "weight": 2 }`
235	  (shares of what fixed siblings leave), `min` / `max` (px), `hidden`.
236	- Paint: `background` (a color; `{ "gradient": ["#2a6cbd", "#0b2a57"], "angle": 165 }`;
237	  or `{ "image": "backgrounds/sky.jpg", "fit": "cover" | "contain" }`, a path in
238	  the home folder), `border` (`{ "width": 1, "color": "border" }`), `radius`,
239	  `shadow` (`"sm" | "md" | "lg"`), `focus` (`{ "border": {...} }` when the
240	  focused pane is inside).
241	- `padding`: space inside the node's edge, px: `16` or `[vertical, horizontal]`.
242	- row/column: `gap` (px between children), `divider` (`{ "width": 1, "color": "border" }`),
243	  `resizable` (default true: drag the boundary). This applies to that row/column only.
244	- `movable` (default true): panes can be dragged by the app's top-center grip within a split tab.
245	  Unlike `resizable`, it inherits: the nearest explicit ancestor wins, through the
246	  tab tree and then the layout's tab block and its ancestors. Root `"movable": false`
247	  opts the layout out. Composition terminal blocks aren't tab panes and never drag.
248	  Center drop swaps panes; an edge drop places beside it. Escape or dropping outside
249	  another pane cancels. Zoomed tabs and one-pane tabs don't drag. The grip appears
250	  on top-edge hover, regardless of the header's position or presence. Only the grip
251	  starts dragging; header mods don't need drag handlers. `panes()` exposes `movable`.
252	- `floating`: blocks over this node (below).
253	- `window_drag: true`: dragging the node moves the window, a double-click
254	  maximizes it. A mod's own control inside opts out by stopping the press:
255	  `.on_mouse_down("left", (_e, cx) => cx.stop_propagation())`.
256	- Root only: `"titlebar": "none"` hides the system title bar so the layout
257	  draws its own (a bar mod in a `window_drag` block). macOS keeps its window
258	  buttons over the layout at `"traffic_lights": [x, y]` (px); leave them
259	  room. Where the system draws no buttons (`window().buttons`, Linux and
260	  Windows), the bar draws them with `window.minimize`, `window.maximize`, `window.close`.
261	  Windows' shipped tab bar and system strip use vector window icons, with a
262	  restore icon when maximized, rather than font glyphs.
263	- Root only: `"preview": "layouts/<name>.svg"` (or png): the picture the
264	  settings screen shows for this layout. Draw one when you make a layout;
265	  without it the person sees a plain frame. New layouts and `themes/*.json`
266	  show up in settings by themselves.
267	- Root only: `"terminal_menu": "my-menu"` chooses the mod for terminal
268	  right-clicks (including Shift+right-click). Omit it for the shipped `menu`;
269	  an unknown mod logs a warning and falls back to `menu`. Clone a shipped
270	  layout before changing this field. Other menus are unchanged.
271	- Root only: `"toast": "my-toast"` chooses the mod that shows notifications
272	  (Herdr's own and every `notify()`), in place of the shipped `toast`; an
273	  unknown mod logs a warning and falls back to `toast`. It gets the same
274	  `props()`: `{title, body, level, icon, action, timeout, overlay}` (`timeout`
275	  is optional). A mod that hands them to the system instead
276	  (`exec("notify-send", ...)`) closes itself at once
277	  with `closeOverlay(props().overlay)`.
278	- Colors are theme names (`border`, `accent`, `surface`, ...) or `#rrggbb[aa]`.
279	
280	A personal terminal menu replaces the whole menu; it doesn't merge items.
281	Create `mods/my-menu/main.js` and `mod.json` (e.g.
282	`{"place":"none","overlay":{"width":280,"height":100}}`), then set the layout root's
283	`"terminal_menu": "my-menu"`. It opens as a pointer popup, default 220×260 px;
284	its `mod.json` overlay width/height override those defaults. It gets
285	`props()` = `{tab: "pane", target: {pane, terminal}, overlay}`. Always use
286	`target.terminal` or `target.pane` in actions, not the focused terminal:
287	right-clicking a different terminal must act on the one clicked. A terminal
288	shown outside a tab (a layout terminal block, a window) has no pane:
289	`target.pane` is its block's id, not in `panes()`, so leave out pane items
290	there, as the shipped menu does. For example:
291	
292	```js
293	import { View, div } from "gpui-kit";
294	import { props, run, closeOverlay } from "herdr";
295	export default class MyMenu extends View {
296	  render() {
297	    return div().id("split-target").child("Split this pane").on_click(() => {
298	      const {target, overlay} = props();
299	      closeOverlay(overlay);
300	      run("pane.split", {pane: target.pane, direction: "right"});
301	    });
302	  }
303	}
304	```
305	
306	### The look: on the layout, cascading
307	
308	A layout's own look wins; settings.json fills what it leaves unset.
309	The theme picker overrides both. These go
310	on any node, and the nearest node up the tree wins, so the root sets the
311	layout's look and a block can differ:
312	
313	```json
314	{ "id": "root", "type": "row", "theme": "graphite", "colors": { "accent": "#a7b4c6" },
315	  "font": "Geist Mono", "font_size": 15, "ui_font": "Geist",
316	  "terminal_padding": [10, 6], "terminal_opacity": 1, ... }
317	```
318	
319	- `theme`: `graphite`, `ink`, `moss` (dark), `paper` (light), or the name
320	  of a file in `themes/`; or one for each appearance:
321	  `"theme": { "light": "paper", "dark": "graphite" }` follows the system's
322	  light or dark mode (or the person's `appearance`). `app.theme {name}`
323	  sets the half of the name's lightness. A layout without a theme shows
324	  settings.json's theme, else graphite or paper. `colors` overrides any theme color by name (see
325	  `theme()` below), for terminals and panels alike: overrides apply in
326	  both appearances, so name theme colors (`chrome`, `canvas`) rather than
327	  writing hex when a layout should work light and dark.
328	- `themes/<name>.json`: `{ "background", "foreground", "selection",
329	  "cursor"?, "ansi": [16 colors], "colors"?: {...} }`, all `#rrggbb`; panel
330	  colors are derived from these, `colors` overrides them. Herdr ships
331	  `atom-one-dark`. The original unedited Atom One Dark and Win98 theme files
332	  are upgraded to readable terminal colors; edited theme files are kept.
333	  A theme named like a layout (`themes/win98.json`) is
334	  that layout's own: Settings offers it only there.

357	
358	The tab block says how each pane of the shown tab is wrapped:
359	
360	```json
361	{ "tab": "active",
362	  "pane": { "gap": 6, "radius": 6, "background": "surface",
363	            "border": { "width": 1, "color": "border" }, "focus": { "width": 1, "color": "accent" },
364	            "header": { "content": { "mod": "pane" }, "height": 30, "position": "top", "reveal": "always" },
365	            "lone": false } }

367	
368	- The look applies to every pane; `focus` replaces the border while the
369	  pane has the keyboard; `gap` is the space between panes.
370	- `header`: a mod drawn on each pane, one copy per pane, with
371	  `props().pane` and `props().terminal`. It reads its live facts from
372	  `panes()` (title, folder, branch, agent status, focused, zoomed) and its
373	  buttons run pane commands with that pane (`pane.split`, `pane.zoom`,
374	  `pane.close`). `position`: `top` or `bottom`; `reveal: "hover"` shows it
375	  only while the pointer is on the pane, drawn over the terminal so the
376	  terminal never resizes. The shipped `pane` mod keeps its divider on the
377	  terminal-facing edge and reads the frame position from `layout()`.
378	- `lone: true` frames a tab's only pane too (default: only when split).
379	- Each layout has its own, so one can stay bare while another makes

382	### Floating blocks
383	
384	```json
385	"floating": [ { "id": "board", "content": { "mod": "board" }, "edge": "left", "align": "center", "peek": 52 } ]
386	```
387	
388	A floating block sits over its node, `edge` (`top`, `right`, `bottom`,
389	`left`) and `align` along it (`start`, `center`, `end`), 12 px in. It sizes
390	to its content (render nothing to hide it). People drag it anywhere; on
391	release it springs to the nearest edge and third, and Herdr saves the new
392	spot. Clicks and hovers on it never reach what's underneath.
393	
394	`peek` (side edges only) makes it a drawer: only that many px next to the
395	edge show until it's hovered, then the rest slides out; it slides back a
396	moment after the pointer leaves. The mod draws one full layout and never
397	changes it on hover (that's what keeps it smooth): put what should peek
398	(status, icons) on the edge side of each row.
399	
400	Herdr draws the frame around a floating mod (theme background, border,
401	rounded corners, shadow; accent border while dragged), like a dialog's,
402	with 5 px above and below. The mod draws only its content, no panel: on a
403	side, rows can run edge to edge. It reads `placement()`:
404	`{ edge, align, vertical, hovered, dragging }`. Lay out vertically when
405	`vertical` (left/right edges), horizontally otherwise; on the right edge,
406	mirror rows so their edge side is on the right.

434	People share layouts at herdr.dev/layouts and mods at herdr.dev/mods. Each

441	folder on GitHub):
442	
443	1. Read the recipe and every file before writing anything. Before adding,
444	   tell the person if a mod reaches the network, runs programs (`exec`,
445	   `hc`) or reads files outside its own folder.
446	2. Copy the layout file to `layouts/` and each mod folder to `mods/`. Leave
447	   the recipe and preview out. Never overwrite: if a name is taken (yours
448	   or Herdr's), rename the new one: its file or folder, the `mod` names in
449	   the layout, and the mod's own `mods/<name>/` paths.
450	3. Fit it to this setup only where its assumptions don't hold (a missing
451	   program, a name clash) or the person asks. If the files don't work on
452	   this version, or the person wants it different, build it from the

454	4. A mod's `keys.json`: merge it into the person's. Add its sections and

458	   and deleting the files removes it.

460	To share one: put that folder in a public GitHub repo (one folder each if
461	there are several), write its `RECIPE.md`, save a screenshot of it as
462	`preview.png` and add the repo topic `herdr-layout` for a layout or
463	`herdr-mod` for a mod. It shows up at herdr.dev/layouts or herdr.dev/mods
464	within the hour.

466	A `RECIPE.md` is a brief: another agent with an empty folder builds the
467	layout or mod from it. Write it from the real files, in this order:
468	
469	1. `# Name`, one paragraph of what the person sees, `![Name](preview.png)`.
470	2. **What you see:** the regions top to bottom or left to right, their
471	   sizes, colors and type; what each one shows.

477	5. **Watch out:** what tripped the build up and what a fresh build would

487	## Keys: `keys.json`
488	
489	On upgrade, an untouched keys file from an earlier release gets the current
490	shortcuts. Any edit, even whitespace, keeps the entire file as yours; new default
491	shortcuts must then be added by hand.
492	
493	```json
494	{
495	  "global":   { "ctrl-shift-t": "tab.new", "ctrl-shift-o": "pane.split:right", "alt-1": "space.select:1" },
496	  "terminal": { "ctrl-shift-c": "terminal.copy", "ctrl-left": "send:\u001bb", "ctrl-1": "terminal" },
497	  "layout:terminals": { "ctrl-shift-pagedown": "space.next", "ctrl-shift-pageup": "space.prev" },
498	  "mod:editor": { "ctrl-s": "editor.save" }
499	}
500	```
501	
502	- Sections: `global`, `layout:<name>` (while `layouts/<name>.json` shows),
503	  `terminal` (a terminal has focus), `mod:<name>`. The more specific section
504	  wins: `layout:terminals` over `global`, `terminal` over both.
505	- An action is a command (`name`, or `name:value`: the value fills the
506	  command's first argument), `send:<text>` (types into the terminal),
507	  `<mod>.<command>` (delivered to that mod's `nextCommand()`), or `terminal`
508	  (the program gets the key).
509	- Named, typed command arguments use an object instead of a string:
510	  `"ctrl-shift-r": {"command": "layout.resize", "args": {"id": "sidebar", "px": 240}}`.
511	  `command` names an app command; `args` is an object (optional, defaults to `{}`).
512	  It can pass several arguments, numbers, booleans, arrays or nested objects.
513	  String actions keep their literal first-argument shorthand, including numeric
514	  indexes: `space.new:{work}` names a space `{work}`, and `space.new:{}` names it `{}`.
515	  Invalid binding objects or rejected arguments show an error toast when pressed;
516	  the key does not go to the terminal program.
517	- Plain ctrl+letters go to the program unless bound. Programs rely on
518	  ctrl+c, ctrl+d, ctrl+l, ctrl+r, ctrl+w, ctrl+a, ctrl+e, ctrl+u, ctrl+k,
519	  ctrl+z and ctrl+[ (Escape); ctrl+alt is AltGr on Windows; option+digits
520	  and letters type characters on many Mac keyboards (`[`, `@`). Don't pick
521	  these on your own. If the person asks for one, bind it and tell them what
522	  it takes from typing.
523	- Windows AltGr and dead-key compositions type text in terminals. macOS
524	  dead keys compose accents through native text input; Option keeps its
525	  keyboard-layout characters rather than acting as Alt.
526	- On macOS, shifted punctuation shortcuts accept both spellings from the
527	  current layout: `cmd-shift-]` and `cmd-}` match the same US-layout keypress.
528	  Existing `keys.json` files don't need to change.
529	- Terminal keys honor the program's negotiated Kitty mode, including on Windows.
530	- Windows terminal Escape stays separate from the following key.
531	- Search: `ctrl-shift-f` (Cmd-F on macOS) opens a find bar inside the focused terminal;
532	  Enter/Shift-Enter moves through matches and Escape closes it while the find field
533	  has focus. Clicking the terminal puts typing, including Escape, back in the program;
534	  the bar and its matches stay.
535	  Each terminal keeps its own query, and reopening selects it so typing replaces it. Search covers the screen and scrollback without replacing text selection.

537	## Commands
538	
539	The one way to change anything; keys, mods (`run(name, args)`), menus and
540	you use the same list. `herdr-app commands` prints every one with its arguments
541	(which are required) and what it does. Unknown argument names are errors and list
542	valid names; they never fall back to the current target. For example, closing a
543	space uses `herdr-app do space.close --id <id> --confirmed true`, not `--space`.
544	Target IDs (`id`, `pane`, `space`, `terminal`) must be strings. Other non-null
545	types are rejected before a current-target default applies; null means omitted.
546	The main ones:
547	
548	- Spaces: `space.new {name?, folder?, tab?, argv?, task?, machine?}`
549	  (machine: another machine from `hc machine ls`; omitted: the focused space's
550	  machine for keys and clicks, this computer for scripts; `""`: this computer.
551	  The space lives there, its
552	  terminals start in that machine's home unless folder, and its tabs and
553	  splits stay there; `spaces()` gives each space's `machine`, null here),
554	  `space.close {id?, confirmed?}`, `space.rename {id?, name}` ("": Herdr's name again),
555	  `space.move {id, index}`, `space.select {index | id}`, `space.next`, `space.prev`.
556	  With no `argv`, the target core chooses that machine's default shell (PowerShell 7 when available on Windows).
557	- Tabs: `tab.new {name?, space?, folder?, argv?, task?}` (argv: an
558	  agent to run, task: its first message). Agents run in your interactive
559	  shell (including fish), which stays open after the agent exits. A terminal
560	  that exits with a nonzero code within two seconds of launch shows an error
561	  toast with its exit code and last output lines. Or `tab.new {name?, space?, mod,
562	  props?}` for a tab whose only pane is a mod (a file, a board; split a shell
563	  in beside it like any tab), `tab.close {id?, confirmed?}` (closing the last tab
564	  closes its space and asks first unless confirmed),
565	  `tab.rename {id?, name}` ("": its number again), `tab.move {id, index}`,
566	  `tab.select {index | id}`, `tab.next`, `tab.prev`,
567	  `tab.settle {id?}`, `tab.unsettle {id?}` (index, next and prev
568	  skip settled tabs).
569	- Panes: `pane.split {direction: "right" | "down", pane?, argv? | mod?, props?}` (a new
570	  terminal, or a mod pane), `pane.close {pane?}`,
571	  `pane.zoom {pane?}`, `pane.focus {pane | terminal}`, `pane.go {direction}`,
572	  `pane.swap {pane?, direction | target}`.
573	  `pane.go` prefers the most recently focused pane along the nearest edge in that
574	  direction; unvisited panes fall back to overlap, then top/left layout order.
575	  `pane.go` also reaches visible mods whose `mod.json` says `"focusable": true`, and
576	  starts from that mod while it holds the keyboard.
577	  `pane.swap {direction}` uses geometry only. Focus history lasts until the window closes.
578	  `pane.swap {target}` trades the places of `pane` (default: the focused one) and
579	  `target`, another pane of the same tab; give `direction` or `target`, not both.
580	  A swap moves panes, not focus: the focused pane stays focused in its new place.
581	  `pane.focus {terminal}` prefers the first visible layout terminal block showing that
582	  address, then its model pane. Clicking a terminal block focuses it too.
583	  While a layout terminal block is focused, implicit split/close/zoom/go/swap and
584	  `terminal.show` fail, as do `terminal.open`/`terminal.keep` with place right/down.
585	  They never act on the terminal's source pane. An explicit `pane` still targets that
586	  model pane; composition edits belong to the mod (edit its layout instead).
587	- Terminals: `terminal.open {argv?, folder?, place?, name?}` (`folder` sets the
588	  starting directory for tabs and right/down splits, with or without `argv`), `terminal.kill {terminal}`,
589	  `terminal.keep {terminal, place?}`, `terminal.park {terminal}`,
590	  `terminal.peek {terminal}` (peek over the tab, with keep-as-tab and close),
591	  `terminal.show {terminal?, pane?}`, `terminal.search` (screen and scrollback;
592	  find bar state stays with that terminal), `terminal.copy`, `terminal.paste` (copied
593	  files, such as Finder's or a clipboard manager's image, as if dropped; an image
594	  alone as `terminal.paste_image` pastes it), `terminal.paste_image` (Ctrl+V: an
595	  image, into a terminal on another machine: copied there, its path pasted; on
596	  Windows, clipboard text is pasted; otherwise Ctrl+V goes to the program, which
597	  reads the clipboard itself). TIFF and BMP clipboard
598	  images are converted to PNG before sending,
599	  `terminal.right_click {to: "program" | "menu", terminal?}` (where right-clicks go
600	  when the program takes the mouse; kept as its label `herdr.right-click=program`;
601	  Shift+right-click is always Herdr's menu),
602	  `terminal.scroll {lines | pages | to: "top" | "bottom", terminal?}` (moves Herdr's view of the
603	  history, not the program: negative lines or pages go up, toward history; pages may be
604	  fractional, one page is the terminal's rows; on the alternate screen, such as vim or less,
605	  there is no history, so nothing moves),
606	  `terminal.pin {terminal, pinned}` (pins an agent to the top of the agent lists;
607	  kept on the terminal as `herdr.pinned`, so every Herdr client shows it, and
608	  gone when the terminal ends; read it as `agents()` `pinned`). Copy, paste, paste-image and implicit
609	  right-click targeting follow keyboard focus, including peek and floating terminals;
610	  with no terminal holding keyboard focus, they use the focused pane or block.
611	  Dragging a text selection past the terminal's top or bottom scrolls while held;
612	  releasing stops it. Programs that track the mouse still get their mouse events
613	  (hold Shift to select text instead). A drag stays with the terminal where it
614	  started, including its release outside the pane; other panes don't receive it.
615	  Terminals display Kitty graphics, including Unicode placeholder images used by
616	  programs such as yazi; partial images and scrolling follow the placeholder cells.
617	- Agents: `agent.next`, `agent.prev`, `agent.focus {terminal}`.
618	- Layout: `layout.switch {name?}`, `layout.toggle {id}`, `layout.show {id}`, `layout.hide {id}`,

658	## The person: `settings.json`
659	
660	What's about the user, never a look:
661	
662	```json
663	{ "zoom": 1, "sounds": { "enabled": true } }
664	```
665	
666	- `zoom` scales the whole app: terminals, mods, the layout's px sizes
667	  (0.5 to 3; the zoom keys change it). Write sizes as designed at zoom 1.
668	- `sounds`: `{ "enabled": true, "done": "<file>", "blocked": "<file>" }`.
669	  When an agent needs the person, or finishes while they aren't looking at
670	  it, Herdr plays a sound and (unless they're looking) posts a toast that
671	  goes there when clicked. `done` / `blocked` replace the bundled MP3s
672	  (path absolute or relative to `~/.config/herdr-app`). Changes apply live,
673	  including the Play buttons in Settings > Alerts.
674	- `core`: the herdr-core binary to use, when it isn't where Herdr looks
675	  (PATH, the login shell's PATH, `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew, mise, Nix,
676	  cargo). Read at start.
677	- `font`, `font_size`, `ui_font`: used where the layout doesn't set its
678	  own. Herdr (main) leaves these unset. Bigger panels: `zoom`.
679	- `font_ligatures`: programming ligatures are off by default; set `true` to
680	  enable them in terminal fonts such as JetBrains Mono and Fira Code. The cursor
681	  and background changes (including selections) break ligatures so individual cells stay clear.
682	- `theme`: a theme name or `{light, dark}`; used where the layout sets none.
683	  The theme picker overrides any layout and stays on that layout.
684	- `colors`: theme color overrides (`{"accent":"#ff8800"}`), with the same
685	  precedence as fonts.
686	- `appearance`: `"light"` or `"dark"` always; absent, the system's. A layout
687	  with a light and a dark theme shows the matching one.

694	  its What's new button opens the waiting update's release range, or this

697	  quiet Updated pill lasts for that launch. A build from source never updates.

699	  media are optional. `update-notes.json` records the last successful app

856	### A mod
857	
858	```js
859	import { View, div } from "gpui-kit";
860	import { v_flex, h_flex } from "gpui-base";
861	import { exec, spaces, theme, run } from "herdr";
862	
863	export default class Branches extends View {
864	  init(_props, cx) {
865	    this.branch = {};
866	    cx.timer.every(3000, (cx) => this.refresh(cx));
867	    this.refresh(cx);
868	  }
869	
870	  refresh(cx) {
871	    cx.spawn(async (cx) => {
872	      for (const p of spaces()) {
873	        // on: a space on another machine runs git there.
874	        const r = await exec("git", ["branch", "--show-current"], { cwd: p.folder, on: p.machine });
875	        this.branch[p.id] = r.stdout.trim();
876	      }
877	      cx.notify();
878	    });
879	  }
880	
881	  render(cx) {
882	    const t = theme();
883	    return v_flex().size_full().bg(t.surface).p(10).gap(4).text_size(13).children(
884	      spaces().map((p) =>
885	        h_flex().id(`b-${p.id}`).gap(8).hover((s) => s.bg(t.raised))
886	          .on_click(() => run("space.select", { id: p.id }))
887	          .child(div().text_color(p.active ? t.foreground : t.muted).child(p.name))
888	          .child(div().text_color(t.dim).child(this.branch[p.id] ?? ""))));
889	  }
890	}
891	```
892	
893	Rules:
894	- `main.js` default-exports a class extending `View`. `init(props, cx)` runs
895	  once; `render(cx)` describes the UI and runs again after `cx.notify()` and
896	  whenever Herdr's live data changes (spaces, agents, terminals, focus,
897	  theme, shared state). Don't poll those.
898	- Module code runs once per source version and is shared by copies, even after all
899	  copies close. Keep instance state and host calls in constructor/init, not module
900	  scope. Each copy still gets its own instance, tasks and localStorage.
901	- **Never keep a `cx` and use it later.** Every callback gets its own:
902	  `on_click((event, cx) => …)`, `cx.spawn(async (cx) => …)`,
903	  `cx.timer.every(ms, (cx) => …)`.
904	- No `setTimeout`/`setInterval` (use `cx.timer`), no top-level `await` (use
905	  `cx.spawn` in `init`). Anything slow goes through `exec` or `fetch`.
906	- Size: put `.id("root").on_size_change((size, cx) => { this.size = size; cx.notify(); })`
907	  on the root `div()`, `h_flex()` or `v_flex()`. It reports `{width, height}`
908	  in logical pixels after the first layout and whenever the size changes,
909	  even with the pointer elsewhere. It does not change `props()`.
910	- Cleanup: an optional `async close(cx)` on the exported `View` gets one final
911	  call when its pane, tab, layout-owned slot or overlay goes, and on app quit.
912	  It is not called for a hidden copy or an inactive tab. Start cleanup inside
913	  `close()`; don't await work started earlier. Await cleanup directly,
914	  for example `async close(cx) { await exec("hc", ["kill", this.browser]); }`.
915	  Closing stays responsive: cleanup has at most 250 ms (shared across copies
916	  on quit), then unfinished tasks are cancelled. On quit, use `exec(...)` and
917	  `run("terminal.kill", { terminal: address })`: those go out before the event
918	  loop stops; other commands may not run. An `exec` already started keeps
919	  running; don't start new long-lived work in `close`. This is best-effort,
920	  not a guarantee after a crash or forced termination.
921	- Use `theme()` colors so the mod follows the user's theme.
922	- **Animate natively, never with a timer.** Every redraw of a mod redraws
923	  the whole window, so `cx.timer.every(90, () => cx.notify())` for a
924	  spinner costs real battery. Use `.frames(["⠋", "⠙", …], 90)` (shows
925	  each string in turn as the element's text), `svg(arc).spin(900)` (turns
926	  an icon once every 900 ms: a ring spinner, e.g.
927	  `mods/workspace-chrome/spinner.svg`), or `.loop("opacity", { from:
928	  0.4, to: 1, period: 1200 })` (also width, height, left, top), and
929	  `.transition(...)` for changes: they run without your script and stop
930	  when not shown. Timers are for data (a clock, a fetch), and only as often
931	  as what they show changes.

962	### The `herdr` module
963	
964	All of it is in `herdr.d.ts`. In short:
965	
966	- Live data: `spaces()` (each with its tabs, status, name, named, folder,
967	  machine, branch), `machines()` (name, null for this computer; layout:
968	  `loading`, `ready`, or `unavailable` on this connection; loading ends on
969	  the first read even if it fails, and offline machines are unavailable),
970	  `agents()` (status, app, space, tab, pinned, focused; "done" turns "idle"
971	  once someone looks at it on any Herdr client), `terminals()`
972	  (every core terminal), `focused()`, `layout()`, `theme()` (every color by
973	  name: background (the terminals', cards), canvas (behind cards), chrome
974	  (sidebars, bars), surface, popover, raised, hover, selected, border,
975	  input (a stronger border), foreground, muted, dim, accent,
976	  accent_foreground, solid and solid_foreground (a primary button),
977	  selection, working, blocked, done, idle, unknown, ansi0..15; light and
978	  dark themes name the same ones), `settings()` (with `dark`: the
979	  appearance now), `keys()`, `commands()` (every app
980	  command, its arguments and what it does), `layouts()` (the layout names).
981	  `focused().agent` is the agent an agent block shows.
982	  `focused().space`/`tab` describe the current window context. With a layout terminal
983	  block focused, `pane` and `shown` are null; `terminal` and `cwd` describe that block,
984	  not its source pane. A terminal in a window (`openOverlay` with a `layout`) that has
985	  the keyboard is reported the same way; pane commands without a `pane` still act on
986	  the focused pane under the window. Check `focused()?.pane` before offering pane controls.
987	  `panes()` still lists only model panes; none is focused while a terminal block is.
988	  For composition navigation: `run("pane.focus", {terminal: nextAddress})`.
989	  Terminal copy/paste and implicit right-click routing follow the focused block.
990	- Floating: `placement()` (null unless this copy floats).
991	- Act: `run(command, args)`.
992	- Overlays: `openOverlay({ mod, props, kind: "dialog" | "popup" | "window", width, height, at, frame })`
993	  returns an id; the mod gets `props().overlay` and closes itself with
994	  `closeOverlay(id)`; Esc closes the top dialog or popup. `frame: "none"`
995	  drops Herdr's border, corners and shadow so the mod draws its own.
996	  `notify({ title, body, level, icon, timeout })` posts a notification, drawn
997	  by the layout-chosen mod (default: `toast`).
998	- Windows (`kind: "window"`): stay open until closed, over the layout and
999	  under dialogs; a press the mod doesn't stop drags it (stop it on your
1000	  controls, like a title bar's buttons), it stays where dropped, and the one
1001	  pressed last is on top. Sized by content unless `width`/`height`; at `at`
1002	  or centered. `key: "name"` remembers its spot (opening that key again
1003	  replaces it); `keep: true` with a key reopens it on the next start. A
1004	  layout switch closes windows; kept ones come back with their layout.
1005	  A window can hold a layout, terminals too: a terminal keeps its presses
1006	  (selecting text), so give it a mod block to drag by, a title bar:
1007	  `openOverlay({ kind: "window", key: "t7", width: 600, height: 400, layout: { type: "column", children: [{ type: "block", size: { px: 28 }, content: { mod: "my-titlebar" } }, { type: "block", content: { terminal: "t7" } }] } })`.
1008	- Machine: `exec(cmd, args, { cwd, on, timeout })` (the user's real environment; use this,
1009	  not `process.run`; `on: space.machine` runs there, omitted means local).
1010	  `timeout` is milliseconds, defaults to 30,000 and is capped at 600,000 (10 minutes),
1011	  locally and remotely. It rejects on timeout, if the program cannot start or the machine cannot be reached.
1012	  `hc(args)` (`hc read <t>` gives a terminal's text),
1013	  `home()`, `appHome()`, `playSound("done" | "blocked" | file)`.
1014	  `knownAgents({ on })`: the agents people can start (programs.json's
1015	  `run`), most picked first, each `installed` or not there (asked of the
1016	  shell agents start in; a remote Unix machine's login/interactive shell when supported);
1017	  rejects if the check fails (failed checks are not cached); start one with `argv: agent.run`.
1018	  `pickFolder({ prompt })`: the system's folder picker (here only),
1019	  resolves with the folder or null.
1020	- Files: `readTextFile(path, { on })` (here, or on that machine),
1021	  `writeTextFile(path, text, expected)` (here only), and
1022	  `watchFolder(dir)` (here only; poll a remote space's folder): resolves with the changed paths the next time anything
1023	  under `dir` changes. On Linux, Git-ignored directories and Git objects are skipped,
1024	  and trees above 4096 non-ignored directories reject the watch; use a timer fallback.
1025	  macOS and Windows watch recursively, including ignored directories.
1026	  A returned root path means refresh everything (the pending paths are bounded).
1027	  Files also refreshes on its 10-second timer:
1028	  `cx.spawn(async (cx) => { for (;;) { await watchFolder(dir); this.reload(); cx.notify(); } })`.

1031	  sees it; setting re-renders all), `nextCommand()` (key commands for this
1032	  mod: `cx.spawn(async (cx) => { for (;;) { const c = await nextCommand(); …; cx.notify(); } })`).

37	## Herdr rules that bite
38	
39	- Herdr runs **`main.js` only** (QuickJS): TypeScript is bundled by esbuild
40	  into one file. `herdr`, `gpui-kit`, `gpui-base` are provided at run time
41	  (externals). No Node APIs, no `setTimeout`, no DOM.
42	- **Never keep a `cx`.** Every callback and task gets its own.
43	- **Never start work in `render()`.** It notices a change (`notice()`) and
44	  fires the `Signal` that the git task started in `init` waits on.
45	- `.when(cond, …)` needs a real boolean.
46	- `exec`: an argument array (no shell), 30 s limit, 8 MiB output, **no stdin**.
47	  Anything that needs input writes a file first (`writeTextFile`, under
48	  `~/.config/herdr-app`). Long operations (clone, big push) belong in a
49	  terminal (`hc`), not `exec`.
50	- Every git call uses `--no-optional-locks`, so gitdeck never blocks an
51	  agent's git in the same repo.

changed: the changed files in the Changes panel, a syntax-highlighted diff
beside them. Press `Enter` and the diff pane _becomes_ your real nvim, at the
line you're on. You never leave Herdr.

## Features

[Permalink: Features](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#features)

- **Takes over the Changes panel** \- the tab bar's **Changes** button (or
`cmd-shift-g`) shows gitview's file list for the space you're in, and a
click opens the file's diff in a full-height pane right beside it. Moving
through the list, the diff follows.
- **Grouped changes** \- conflicts, staged, and unstaged changes in separate
sections, flat or as a folder tree, with `+ added −deleted` counts per file
and in total.
- **Stage, discard, commit inline** \- `s`/`u`/`x` or the `+``−``↺` buttons
on a file, a folder or a whole section; discards confirm first. Write the
commit message right in the panel (`shift+enter` for more lines) and
commit what's staged, or everything when nothing is.
- **Readable diffs** \- syntax highlighting (dark or light, to match your
app theme), added and removed lines tinted in the theme's colors,
word-level emphasis on edited lines, and collapsible context folds.
- **Preview** \- markdown renders, images show, and a changed image shows
before and after side by side. One click switches back to the diff.
- **Edit in real nvim** \- `Enter` turns the diff pane into your nvim, at the
line ( [herdr-nvim](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-nvim)'s when it's
installed). `:q` brings the diff back. Moving to another file swaps nvim
for that file's diff again; with unsaved changes nvim stays.
- **Commit history** \- `l` opens the log; pick a commit to browse its files
and diffs. `w` filters it to the commits your branch added.
- **Knows what your branch was cut from** \- branch scope diffs against the
branch you actually branched off ( [Branch scope](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/TUI.md#branch-scope)).
- **Review notes to any agent** \- select diff lines, write a note under them,
and send the batch into the input of any agent in Herdr. It types, without
the clipboard; you decide when to press enter.
- **A tab of its own** \- `cmd-g` opens gitview in a tab for the repo you're
in: the diff on the left, the list on the right.
- **Remote spaces** \- in a space on another machine, git runs there.
- **Mouse support** \- click, double-click to open, drag-select diff lines,
hover buttons.

## Requirements

[Permalink: Requirements](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#requirements)

- The **Herdr desktop app** (herdr-app ≥ 0.1.12).

## Install

[Permalink: Install](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#install)

With the Herdr app open:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
```

It downloads the prebuilt gitview for your machine, checks it, adds its
mods, adds `cmd-shift-g` and `cmd-g` where they're free, and puts gitview in
the Changes panel. No git clone, no Rust. Or ask the agent in your Herdr
window to "add the mod at github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview".

- **Update:** run the same command again.
- **Uninstall:** the same command with `--uninstall`; the stock Changes
panel comes back.

## Quick start

[Permalink: Quick start](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#quick-start)

1. **Open it.** Press **Changes** in the tab bar, or `cmd-shift-g`. The
space's changed files show in the panel.
2. **Browse.** Click a file, or `j`/`k`: its diff opens in a full-height pane
beside the panel and follows your selection.
3. **Edit.**`Enter` turns the diff pane into nvim at the line. `:q`, and
you're back on the diff.
4. **Stage & commit.**`s` to stage (the file moves up), `x` to discard (asks
first), `c` to write the commit message, `enter` to commit.
5. **See what your branch did.**`w` switches to "vs the base branch"; `l`
opens the log filtered to your branch's commits.
6. **Review for your agent.** In the diff, drag over lines (or `v` +
`j`/`k`), `a` to write a note, `enter` to save it. `p` → pick an agent →
the notes land in its input.

The footer shows the keys that work right now; `?` lists them all.

| `J` / `K` | diff | Next / previous file |
| `v`, `a` | diff | Select lines, write a note |
| `p` | list, diff | Send the notes to an agent |

## Configuration

[Permalink: Configuration](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#configuration)

gitview reads the same `config.toml` as the TUI plugin,
`~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/chmarax.gitview/config.toml`. In the app
these apply: `editor`, `base`, `context_lines`, `show_untracked` and
`view_width_percent` (the diff pane's width). See
[TUI.md](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/TUI.md#configuration) for each key. Colors follow the app's theme.

## Limitations

[Permalink: Limitations](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#limitations)

- **nvim is the editor gitview knows** \- with herdr-nvim's nvim or your own
nvim, gitview checks for unsaved changes and closes it for you. Other
editors open the file too; you close them yourself.
- **Notes attach to working-tree changes** \- you can't annotate historical
commits.
- **herdr-nvim on remote spaces** \- in a space on another machine, Enter
starts a plain editor there instead.

## Development

[Permalink: Development](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#development)

```
git clone https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview
cd herdr-gitview
herdr-app/install.sh               # builds from source and installs into the running app
herdr-app/install.sh --uninstall

`cargo test` runs the engine's tests and `node --test herdr-app/test/*.test.mjs`

`follow.sh`, `jank.sh`, `reload.sh`, `package.sh`) drive a private app in the
background. How the mods are built: [herdr-app/RECIPE.md](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/herdr-app/RECIPE.md).

{"markdown":"# gitview

Review what your agents changed, stage it and commit it, without leaving
Herdr. gitview takes over the Changes panel: it lists the repo's changed
files (staged, unstaged, conflicts; flat or as a tree), and a click opens
the file's diff in a full-height pane beside it. Stage, unstage and discard
with a key or a button, commit from the panel, write review notes on lines
and send them to an agent, and press Enter to edit the file in nvim.

![gitview](preview.png)

## Adding it (for the app's agent)

Don't copy the folders: gitview needs its binary, and it edits the person's
layout (the Changes panel), which copying doesn't do. With the app open,
run its installer:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
```

Tell the person first what it does:

- downloads the prebuilt `herdr-gitview` for this machine from the GitHub
  release, checked against its SHA-256 (macOS and Linux);
- runs programs (`git`, `hc`, `herdr-app`, an editor) and writes to the repo
  only when they stage, discard or commit; no network of its own (a space on
  another machine is reached through herdr-core);
- adds the gitview mods, adds `cmd-shift-g` and `cmd-g` where they are free,
  and points the layout's Changes panel at gitview (on one of Herdr's own
  layouts, a copy of it, which it switches to).

It needs git. Running the installer again upgrades; `--uninstall` takes all
of it out and brings back the stock Changes panel.

## What you see

- **The panel** (the layout's `changes` block), drawn like the stock one: a
  42px header with `uncommitted` (or `vs <base>`), the branch in `muted`, an
  `N notes` pill, a bordered `N files` pill with the `+A −D` totals, a
  spinner place that never moves anything, and from 340px wide tree/flat
  and history buttons.
- **The list**: section headers (Merge conflicts, Staged, Changes) with a
  count chip; 28px file rows with the status letter (M `blocked`, A/U
  `ansi2`, D `ansi1`, R `ansi4`), the folder in `dim`, the name, `+adds`
  `ansi2` and `−dels` `ansi1`. Hover `hover`, selected `selected`. On the
  hovered or selected row the counts give way to `+`, `−` and `↺` buttons; a
  hovered section header shows them for all its files. Tree mode adds folder
  rows (chevron, folder icon, file count), a folder holding one folder folded
  into it.
- **The commit row** (uncommitted view): a message box that grows to 8 lines
  and a button: "Commit staged", or "Commit all" with nothing staged.
- **The footer**: the view's most useful keys as keycaps (`[s] stage [u]
  unstage [⏎] nvim …`) and a `?` keycap for the keys card; a message replaces
  them for 5s. The commit row and the footer stay at the panel's bottom,
  also when the list is empty or loading.
- **History** (`l`): commits with subject, refs, short sha, age and author;
  a commit opens its files. **Notes** (`n`): each note's `file:lines` and
  first line.
- **The diff pane**, full height at the tab's right edge, just left of the
  panel: a header (status, path, `+a −d`, a scope tag: `staged`,
  `uncommitted`, `vs <base>` or `commit <sha>`, ×) and the diff in the
  terminal font: line numbers, syntax colors, inserts and deletes tinted
  `ansi2`/`ansi1` at 15% with changed words at 36%, unchanged runs folded
  (`▸ ⋯ N unchanged lines`). The cursor line is a faint full-width band
  with a 2px bar; colors too dim on a tint are lifted to 3.5 contrast.
  Notes show as cards under their lines. A diff longer than 5,000 lines
  ends with "diff cut at 5,000 lines".
- **Preview**, for markdown, images, SVG and HTML: a `Diff | Preview`
  toggle in the header; markdown rendered, an image fitted, a changed image
  before | after side by side.
- **cmd-g's tab** "gitview": the diff on the left, the list on the right.
- **Dialogs**: "Discard changes?" (the app's confirm), "Send N notes to…"
  (the agents, this space's first), the keys card (`?`), and "Save them?"
  when an editor gitview started has unsaved changes.

## How it behaves

- **The panel follows the shown space**: the repo of the focused terminal's
  folder, else the space's. Focusing gitview's diff pane or herdr-nvim's
  nvim keeps the repo. It refreshes on a folder watch; a space on another
  machine is polled every 4s while gitview has the keys, else every 10s.
- **Browsing**: a click, `j`/`k` or the arrows select a file and its diff
  shows at once; the pane opens on the first file clicked and is reused.
  Between files the old diff stays (dimmed after 150ms) until the new one is
  there: the pane never blanks.
- **List keys**: `s` stage, `u` unstage, `x` discard (asks first) the row,
  folder or section; `enter` opens the file in the editor (on a folder:
  folds it); `h`/`←` and `→` fold and unfold; `t` flat or tree; `w`
  uncommitted or vs base; `l` history; `n` notes; `p` send notes; `c` the
  commit message (enter commits, shift-enter a new line, esc leaves it);
  `g`/`G` first and last; `r` refresh; `?` all keys. Chords with cmd, ctrl
  or alt are left to the app.
- **Diff pane keys**: `j`/`k`, page keys, `g`/`G`, the wheel and clicks move
  the cursor; `v` or a drag selects; `a` writes a note on the selection
  (staged or unstaged diffs only); `s`/`u`/`x` act on the shown file; `J`/`K`
  the next or previous file (the list follows); `m` Diff or Preview; `enter`
  the editor at the cursor's line; `esc` clears the selection.
- **Enter → the editor**, which takes the diff pane's place (as v1's diff
  pane became nvim):
  - the editor: herdr-nvim's nvim when it's installed; else an nvim already
    in the tab; else the one configured (`editor` in config.toml, `$VISUAL`,
    `$EDITOR`, nvim, vim, vi), started in a terminal in the diff's place;
    else the system's opener, in its own window; with no editor, a toast
    says what to install;
  - `:q` brings the diff back on that file with the keys on the list; the
    file's row shows `in nvim`, and a click on it brings the diff back too
    (herdr-nvim keeps the buffer; an nvim gitview started quits when clean);
  - moving to another file: herdr-nvim's pane makes way for the new diff
    (the daemon keeps unsaved edits); an nvim gitview started quits when
    clean and its place goes to the new diff, and stays with "editor has
    unsaved changes — stays open" when not; an editor gitview can't ask
    (vim) stays, and its diff comes when it quits;
  - in cmd-g's tab the diff stays, and the editor opens beside it.
- **Discard** asks first. From Changes it keeps a partly staged file's staged
  part.
- **Commit** commits what's staged, else everything (`git add -A`); with
  conflicts it refuses and changes nothing. A slow hook past 30s says "still
  running or timed out: check git log" and keeps the message.
- **Notes** are kept per repo until sent or deleted. Send places them in the
  agent's input as a bracketed paste (no clipboard), or submits them with
  shift-enter; a program without bracketed paste gets nothing and the dialog
  says why.
- **cmd-shift-g** shows the panel with the keys on the list, or hides it.
  Hiding it (also by the Changes or Files button) closes gitview's unit in
  the space: the diff panes, the herdr-nvim pane gitview handed a file to,
  and an editor gitview started (a clean one quits; unsaved changes ask Save,
  Discard or Cancel). Showing it again opens the selected file. **cmd-g**
  opens the gitview tab for the repo, jumps to it, and from inside closes it.
- **One focus**: the list takes the keyboard through `pane.go right`, so
  only one thing looks focused.
- **Tracing**: gitview keeps a trace of what it did for bug reports (no file
  contents, messages, notes or diff text). The palette has "gitview: mark
  (something's wrong)" and "gitview: tracing on/off".

## Built from

- **Layout**: only the `changes` block of the person's personal layout
  changes, to `{mod: "gitview", props: {replaces: <old content>}}`; the tab
  bar's Changes button then shows gitview. On one of Herdr's own layouts the
  installer clones it once (`<name>-copy`) and switches to the copy. Keys go
  in only where free. Uninstall puts `replaces` back and removes only its
  keys; it never deletes or switches a layout. herdr-nvim edits `files` the
  same way, in either order.
- **Mods**:
  - `gitview`: the list, in the panel and in cmd-g's tab (`placement.js`
    decides which from the props);
  - `gitview-diff`: the diff pane (`props: {tab}`), its Preview, and an image
    cache in `mods/gitview-diff/.cache` (hidden, the newest 50 files);
  - `gitview-sidebar` (cmd-shift-g) and `gitview-tab` (cmd-g): one-shot
    launchers;
  - `gitview-agents` (the send dialog), `gitview-ask` (Save them?),
    `gitview-keys` (the keys card), `gitview-mark` and `gitview-tracing`
    (the palette commands).

  Files the mods share are symlinks in the repo; the installer copies them.
- **The list is the only writer of what the pane shows**: shared
  `gitview.views[<tab>]` (the file, section, scope, base or commit, its
  `rev`, a `seq` per write and a `showing` per new file). The pane asks the
  list for s/u/x and J/K (`gitview.ask` / `gitview.answer`) and publishes its
  cursor (`gitview.cursor`). Other shared keys: `gitview.notes`,
  `gitview.handoff` (the file handed to herdr-nvim), `gitview.editors` (the
  editors gitview started), `gitview.discards` (pending discards by token),
  `gitview.changed` (a repo changed). Per-tab keys drop tabs that are gone.
- **The binary** `mods/gitview/bin/herdr-gitview`, paths in
  `mods/gitview/config.json`:
  `json status|diff|file|stage|unstage|discard|commit|log|commit-files|notes|nvim|editor|send|sidebar`
  and `app-setup install|uninstall`. Every repo op takes `--on <machine>`
  (git runs there through `hc exec --on`) and `--root`. The contract is the
  module doc of `src/appjson.rs`.
- **Keys** (`keys.json`): `cmd-shift-g` gitview-sidebar, `cmd-g`
  gitview-tab; on Linux (`keys.linux.json`) `ctrl-alt-shift-g`,
  `ctrl-alt-g`.
- **Install**: `install.sh` at the repo root (release bundle), or
  `herdr-app/install.sh` in a clone (builds from source).

## Watch out

- Read `props()` only in `init` and keep it: in a task resumed by a promise,
  `props()` can belong to another copy (null 3–12% of the time), and the
  pane skipped files.
- Never start work from `render()`: render notices a change and wakes a task
  made in `init`.
- Rows in the app's virtual lists can't have their own handlers, so the list
  is the mod's own scroller (`scroller.js`).
- A hidden copy (the panel's list while the panel is hidden, or any copy in
  a covered window) isn't drawn: the list also looks every 300ms.
- herdr-app 0.1.12–0.1.13 issues with workarounds in the mods:
  - an exec in flight can be dropped when a mod pane or dialog closes; the
    loads treat it as lost and run again (`Loads.revive`), and a confirmed
    discard still running after 1.5s counts as lost;
  - with two copies waiting on `watchFolder` for one folder, only the newest
    wakes; the waking list stamps `gitview.changed` and every list follows
    it;
  - a copy not waiting on `nextCommand()` when a command comes never gets
    it; one task only queues commands;
  - every hot reload keeps the old code for the app's life: the installer
    swaps each changed mod in with one rename and leaves unchanged ones
    alone;
  - `pane.go` does nothing in a window that never drew.
- `terminal.show` can't put a terminal in a mod pane, so the editor's
  terminal opens right of the diff pane and the diff pane closes, in one
  turn; the copy that ran Enter may be the closing diff pane, so the
  editor's record is written first and any copy finds its terminal.
- Swap panes in one turn (open or split the new one off the old one, then
  close the old), or the terminals widen and narrow again.
- herdr-nvim runs in its daemon's folder: don't take its pane's folder as the
  repo.
- `exec` has a 30s limit and no stdin; every call the engine makes to
  herdr-core, herdr-app or nvim has its own deadline.
- macOS is tested end to end; the app version is untested on Linux (the
  release ships a Linux bundle, and CI tests the engine there); Windows
  isn't supported.

## Done when

- `herdr-app check` passes for every gitview mod and `herdr-app status`
  shows no errors.
- The Changes button shows the shown space's changes; a click opens one diff
  pane beside the panel, and j/k, clicks and J/K reuse it, each move showing

- `s`/`u`/`x` and the buttons change exactly what git says; discard asks
  first; the commit row commits the staged files, or everything with none
  staged, and refuses with conflicts.
- History lists commits and a commit's files; notes show as cards and reach
  an agent's input without the clipboard.
- Enter opens the editor at the line; with herdr-nvim, `:q` brings the diff
  back and moving to another file swaps nvim for its diff.
- cmd-shift-g hides the panel with its unit and shows it with the selected
  file; cmd-g opens, jumps to and closes the gitview tab.
- A markdown file opens in Preview; a changed image shows before and after.
- A space on another machine lists, diffs, stages and edits there.
- An agent's write shows in the list within 2s.
- Uninstall brings back the stock Changes panel and leaves keys.json as it
  was.
- `node --test herdr-app/test/*.test.mjs` and the e2e suites
  (`herdr-app/e2e/run.sh`, `coexist.sh`, `follow.sh`, `jank.sh`,
  `reload.sh`, `package.sh`) pass.

# With neither --app nor --tui: whichever Herdr is installed (both if both).
# Run it again to upgrade.
#
# App: downloads the release's app bundle for this machine (the
# herdr-gitview binary and the mods; no clone, no Rust toolchain), checks it
# against its SHA-256, and runs the bundle's herdr-app/install.sh with the
# app open. --version picks a release (default: the latest), --bundle a
# bundle file instead of a download (its .sha256 beside it is checked).
#
# TUI: `herdr plugin install ChmaraX/herdr-gitview` (or `herdr plugin
# update`); its keys are bound by hand, as TUI.md says.
set -eu

repo=ChmaraX/herdr-gitview
plugin=chmarax.gitview
app= tui= uninstall= version= bundle=
die() { echo "gitview: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "gitview: $*"; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case $1 in
    --app) app=1 ;;
    --tui) tui=1 ;;
    --uninstall) uninstall=1 ;;
    --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--version needs a tag"; version=$2; shift ;;
    --bundle) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--bundle needs a file"; bundle=$2; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,19p' "$0" 2>/dev/null || echo "see https://github.com/$repo#install"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "unknown argument $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done

# The Herdr app: herdr-app on PATH, a Herdr bundle (macOS, by its bundle id),
# or an app home (Linux, or a launch that never put it on PATH).
have_app() {
  command -v herdr-app >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  for b in /Applications/*.app "$HOME"/Applications/*.app; do
    [ -f "$b/Contents/Info.plist" ] || continue
    [ "$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw "$b/Contents/Info.plist" 2>/dev/null)" = dev.herdr.app ] && return 0
  done
  [ -d "${HERDR_APP_HOME:-$HOME/.config/herdr-app}" ]
}
have_tui() { command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1; }

if [ -z "$app$tui" ]; then
  have_app && app=1
  have_tui && tui=1
  [ -n "$app$tui" ] || die "found neither the Herdr app nor the herdr TUI; install one first (https://herdr.dev)"
fi

target() {
  case "$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" in
    Darwin-arm64) echo aarch64-apple-darwin ;;
    Darwin-x86_64) echo x86_64-apple-darwin ;;
    Linux-x86_64) echo x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
    Linux-aarch64|Linux-arm64) echo aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
    *) die "no prebuilt gitview for $(uname -s) $(uname -m); build from source (README: Development)" ;;
  esac
}

sha256() {
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$1"; else sha256sum "$1"; fi | cut -d' ' -f1
}

install_app() {
  work=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
  if [ -n "$bundle" ]; then
    [ -f "$bundle" ] || die "no bundle at $bundle"
    cp "$bundle" "$work/app.tar.gz"
    [ ! -f "$bundle.sha256" ] || cp "$bundle.sha256" "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256"
  else
    name=herdr-gitview-app-$(target).tar.gz
    if [ -n "$version" ]; then base=https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$version
    else base=https://github.com/$repo/releases/latest/download; fi
    say "downloading $name (${version:-latest})"
    curl -fsSL "$base/$name" -o "$work/app.tar.gz" ||
      die "could not download $base/$name (releases before the app bundle have none; build from source: README)"
    curl -fsSL "$base/$name.sha256" -o "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256" || die "could not download $name.sha256"
  fi
  if [ -f "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256" ]; then
    want=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256")
    [ "$(sha256 "$work/app.tar.gz")" = "$want" ] || die "the bundle does not match its SHA-256; nothing installed"
  fi
  tar -xzf "$work/app.tar.gz" -C "$work"
  dir=$(find "$work" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'herdr-gitview-app-*' | head -1)
  [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -x "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" ] || die "the bundle has no bin/herdr-gitview"
  # The binary runs here (`json` with no op answers in JSON); no answer (an
  # older glibc, another architecture) means it can't.
  "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" json 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"error"' ||
    die "the prebuilt herdr-gitview does not run on this machine; build from source (README: Development)"
  bash "$dir/herdr-app/install.sh" --binary "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" ${uninstall:+--uninstall}
}

install_tui() {
  command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "the herdr TUI is not installed (https://herdr.dev)"
  listed=$(herdr plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -F -- "- $plugin " || true)
  if [ -n "$uninstall" ]; then
    [ -n "$listed" ] || { say "the TUI plugin is not installed"; return; }
    herdr plugin uninstall "$plugin"
    say "removed the TUI plugin"
  elif echo "$listed" | grep -q '\[local:'; then
    say "the TUI plugin is linked from a checkout ($listed); left as it is"
  elif [ -n "$listed" ]; then
    herdr plugin update --yes "$plugin"
    say "updated the TUI plugin"
  else
    herdr plugin install --yes "$repo"
    say "installed the TUI plugin; bind its keys in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml (https://github.com/$repo/blob/main/TUI.md#install)"
  fi
}

[ -z "$app" ] || install_app
[ -z "$tui" ] || install_tui

// Builds the mod folder dist/gitdeck/: one bundled main.js plus mod.json and assets.
// One file means one reload when installed (each reload keeps old code alive in herdr-app 0.1.x).
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { cp, mkdir, readFile, rm } from "node:fs/promises";

const out = "dist/gitdeck";
const { version } = JSON.parse(await readFile("package.json", "utf8"));

await rm(out, { recursive: true, force: true });
await mkdir(out, { recursive: true });

await build({
  entryPoints: ["src/main.ts"],
  outfile: `${out}/main.js`,
  bundle: true,
  format: "esm",
  target: "es2022",
  platform: "neutral",
  // Provided by the Herdr runtime.
  external: ["herdr", "gpui-kit", "gpui-base", "gpui", "gpui-shell", "fs/promises"],
  // The installed version, for the update check (src/updater.ts).
  define: { __GITDECK_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(version) },
  legalComments: "none",
  logLevel: "warning",
});

await cp("mod/mod.json", `${out}/mod.json`);
await cp("mod/icons", `${out}/icons`, { recursive: true });
process.stdout.write(`build: ${out}\n`);

✅ MoAI-Easy ★ 다 됐어요 ──────────────────────
🎯 Goal: Herdr mod을 다른 언어로 만들 수 있는지 분석하고, gitdeck에 맞는 선택을 추천하는 보고서
📁 Files: 코드는 하나도 바꾸지 않았습니다. `git status`가 작업 시작 때와 같습니다.
🧪 Proof: 아래 "직접 측정한 것"에 명령과 출력을 적었습니다.
──────────────────────────────────────────────

## 결론

**TypeScript를 그대로 유지하길 권합니다.** Rust나 Go로 mod 전체를 만드는 길은 막혀 있습니다. 대신 JS가 UI를 그리고 Rust·Go 바이너리가 일을 하는 혼합 구조는 가능합니다. 그런데 gitdeck에는 그 이득이 비용보다 작습니다.

## 1. Herdr는 mod를 어떻게 불러오나

**확인한 사실**
- mod는 JavaScript입니다. `main.js`가 `View` 클래스를 export하면, 화면 요소(GPUI element)를 *설명*만 하고 Rust 쪽이 실제로 그립니다 (`~/.config/herdr-app/AGENTS.md` 39~47행).
- 이 저장소의 `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`는 실행 환경을 QuickJS(아주 작은 JS 엔진)로 적고 있습니다. Herdr 자체 문서에는 이 이름이 없고, 이 저장소 문서에만 있는 내용입니다.
- `herdr.d.ts`와 `gpui-kit.d.ts`에서 wasm, native, ffi, dylib를 찾아봤지만 mod 로딩과 관련된 항목이 없었습니다.
- 임시 폴더의 mod를 `herdr-app check`(herdr-app 0.1.15)로 돌려 봤더니 `typeof WebAssembly`가 `undefined`였습니다.
- 외부 프로그램은 `exec(cmd, args, {cwd, on, timeout})`로 실행합니다. 기본 30초, 최대 10분, 출력 8 MiB, stdin 없음입니다. 문서도 "mod는 신뢰된 코드이고 명령·네트워크가 제한 없다"고 명시합니다.

**결론**: Herdr가 직접 불러오는 것은 JS뿐입니다. WASM이나 네이티브 플러그인 로딩 경로는 문서에도 런타임에도 없었습니다. Rust·Go는 `exec`로 부르는 별도 프로그램으로만 쓸 수 있습니다.

## 2. 다른 사람들은 무엇으로 만드나

**확인한 사실** (GitHub 토픽 `herdr-mod`, 2026-11-13 기준 695개 저장소)

| 대표 언어 | 개수 | 비율 |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | 595 | 약 86% |
| Python | 45 | 약 6% |
| **Rust** | **18** | **약 2.6%** |
| **Go** | **15** | **약 2.2%** |
| TypeScript | 14 | 약 2% |

Rust mod가 많다는 인상은 사실과 다릅니다. 압도적으로 JS입니다.

실제로 열어 본 두 사례는 둘 다 "JS 껍데기 + 별도 바이너리" 구조입니다.
- **herdr-gitview** (Rust 68%, JS 20%). gitdeck와 같은 종류의 git 패널입니다. UI는 JS mod 여러 개가 그리고, 일은 `mods/gitview/bin/herdr-gitview` 바이너리가 `status`, `diff`, `stage`, `commit` 같은 하위 명령으로 처리합니다. JS가 `exec`로 호출하는 구조입니다. 설치는 OS·CPU별 바이너리를 내려받아 SHA-256을 확인하는 스크립트이고, macOS(arm64·x64)와 Linux(x64·arm64)만 지원합니다. Windows는 미지원입니다. RECIPE.md에는 "폴더를 복사하지 말고 설치 스크립트를 쓰라"고 적혀 있습니다.
- **herdr-auto-title** (Go). 데스크톱용 JS mod가 릴리스 바이너리를 내려받아 SHA256SUMS를 확인한 뒤 `desktop install`을 실행합니다. `exec`의 30초 제한 때문에 설치를 별도 탭에서 돌린다고 커밋 메시지에 적혀 있습니다.

**한계**: Rust·Go 33개 중 위 둘만 열어 봤습니다. 이 토픽에는 데스크톱 앱 mod 외에 herdr TUI(터미널판) 플러그인과 layout도 섞여 있고, 두 사례는 `herdr-plugin.toml`을 가진 TUI 플러그인도 겸합니다. 나머지 Rust·Go가 어느 쪽인지는 확인하지 못했습니다.

## 3. 비교

| 항목 | TS 유지 | Rust 엔진 + JS UI | Go 엔진 + JS UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| 성능 | 병목은 git 프로세스 기동입니다. 측정은 안 했습니다 | 큰 diff 파싱·그래프 계산에서 이득이 *있을 수 있음* (추측) | Rust와 비슷 (추측) |
| 배포 | `main.js` 하나(202 KB), OS 무관 | OS·CPU별 빌드 4종 이상, 설치 스크립트 필요 | 같음 |
| 자동 업데이트 | 지금 방식 그대로 동작 | JS와 바이너리의 버전을 같이 맞춰야 함 | 같음 |
| 테스트 | 326개 통과, 이미 구축 | 엔진 테스트 재작성, JS UI는 계속 별도 | 같음 |
| 이전 작업량 | 없음 | 엔진 이전 + JSON 계약 + CI + 설치기, 두 언어 유지 | 같음 |
| 보안 | 읽을 수 있는 JS만 설치 | 서명 안 된 바이너리를 내려받아 실행 | 같음 |

**근거**
- **성능**: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`가 git 호출이 대부분임을 보여 줍니다. 언어를 바꿔도 git 자체의 시간은 줄지 않습니다. 이득이 있다면 JS에서 하는 파싱 쪽인데, 실제로 느린지는 재 보지 않았습니다.
- **배포**: `scripts/build.mjs`가 `dist/gitdeck/main.js` 하나를 만듭니다(202 KB 측정). 바이너리가 생기면 gitview처럼 OS별 빌드와 체크섬이 필요합니다. macOS 빌드를 위해 `macos-15`와 `macos-15-intel` 러너를 따로 쓴 사례가 있습니다.
- **업데이트**: `src/updater.ts`는 하루 한 번 GitHub 릴리스를 확인하고, 클릭하면 tar.gz를 받아 `herdr-app check`로 검사한 뒤 한 번의 `mv`로 교체합니다. JS 파일만 바꾸는 구조라서 바이너리가 끼면 다시 설계해야 합니다. 읽은 범위(1~80행)에는 체크섬 검증이 없습니다.
- **테스트**: 아래 측정 참고. 이전하면 `src/core`의 순수 로직은 옮기기 쉬운 구조입니다. 하지만 `ui/`와 `main.ts`는 JS로 남고, 그쪽은 `herdr-app check`와 스크린샷으로만 확인합니다.
- **보안**: AGENTS.md는 외부 mod를 추가할 때 "모든 파일을 읽고, 네트워크·프로그램 실행 여부를 알리라"고 합니다. 바이너리는 이 절차로 읽을 수 없습니다(제 해석입니다). 이 워크로드에서는 JS도 Go도 Rust도 메모리 안전성 차이가 실익이 아닙니다.

**직접 측정한 것**
```
pnpm test      → tests 326 / pass 326 / fail 0 / 3.86초
pnpm coverage  → all files: lines 99.70 / branches 94.98 / funcs 98.25
find src -name '*.ts' | wc → 7,348줄 (tests 3,871줄)
```

## 4. 추천

**TypeScript 유지.** 이유 세 가지입니다.
1. 지금 구조(JS 한 파일, 하루 한 번 점검, 원자적 교체)가 Herdr의 설치·갱신 방식과 정확히 맞습니다. 바이너리를 넣으면 이 장점이 사라집니다.
2. 성능 문제가 실제로 있다는 증거가 아직 없습니다. 같은 종류의 mod 중 git-graph, Better Changes, Redline은 JS입니다(언어 표시만 확인).
3. 이전의 대가는 두 언어 유지, OS별 빌드, 보안 면적 증가입니다.

**다시 검토할 신호**: 거대한 저장소(커밋 수만 개 이상)에서 JS 파싱이 체감될 만큼 느리거나, `exec`의 30초·8 MiB 제한에 실제로 걸릴 때입니다. 그때도 전체를 옮기지 말고 병목 한 곳만 작은 바이너리로 빼는 편이 낫습니다. 굳이 고르면 단일 정적 바이너리라 교차 빌드가 쉬운 Go가 유리해 보이지만, 이건 일반 지식이고 이 조사로 검증한 것은 아닙니다.

## 확인하지 못한 것 (추측으로 남은 부분)
- Rust·Go 엔진이 실제로 몇 배 빠른지: 벤치마크를 하지 않았습니다.
- `exec` 한 번의 기동 비용: 재지 않았습니다.
- 내려받은 바이너리가 macOS Gatekeeper(서명 검사)에서 막히는지: 확인하지 않았습니다.
- QuickJS가 WASM을 지원하는지: Herdr 런타임에서 `WebAssembly`가 없는 것만 확인했습니다.
